corpusSummary: Across 2026 records, scholars investigate how large language models shape human–AI interactions, governance, education, and research practice. Findings reveal nuanced trust dynamics and embodiment limits, while LLMs serve as methodological partners for analysis, simulation, and public participation. The literature highlights opportunities for AI-enabled learning and decision-making alongside caution about bias, misinformation, and sustainability.

themes.name: Trust, embodiment, and human–AI interaction
themes.description: A cluster of studies investigates trust, perceived humanness vs. empathy, AI embodiment, and user attitudes across health, education, and everyday decision contexts.

themes.name: LLMs as methodological partners: analysis, simulation, and governance
themes.description: Papers explore using LLMs to assist content analysis, coding, data classification, multi-agent simulations, and public-participation processes, while stressing validation, transparency, and ethical governance.

themes.name: AI in education and learning: pedagogy, assessment, and equity
themes.description: A body of work examines AI’s role in STEM education, language learning, tutoring, and assessment design, with attention to trust, privacy, workload, and digital divide.

themes.name: Safety, bias, and misinformation in AI outputs
themes.description: Studies assess accuracy, safety, fairness, and the spread of misinformation in AI-generated content across health, media, and library contexts, often highlighting risks and mitigation strategies.

emergingKeywords: ethics, bias, and fairness in AI outputs
